newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM sees 15 pct return on investment in 96.
newsitem.headline: DSM sees 15 pct return on investment in 96.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM NV said on Thursday it expected to achieve a return on investment of about 15 percent for 1996.
In an interview with the company's staff magazine, chairman Simon De Bree said:

"We have said before that 1996 would be a good year in financial terms. And we still think so. We expect to record a good result, with a significant increase in sales compared with last year. Our return on investment operating result as a percentage of average capital employed will be around 15 percent, which is what we aim for."
Extracts from interview with DSM chairman Simon de Bree:
"DSM is well-placed to deliver a better performance. Thanks to the drastic restructuring we carried out in our Concern 2000 project, our efficiency and productivity have both improved significantly."

"Apart from an improved organisational structure, we also have a clear strategy: defending and strengthening our strong positions in petrochemicals (polymers and chemicals) and expanding our positions in fine chemicals, performance materials and plastic products."

"Instead of using the term 'shareholders value', we prefer to speak of 'business value', to indicate that the long-term growth and profitability of our business are of paramount importance. And we are convinced that our shareholders also stand to gain by this policy."

"All our business groups have indentified attractive opportunities in the market and have planned new investments and acquisistions for the coming years involving an expenditure of on average more than one billion guilders a year."
